name: EyeShadows
summary: Gaze-only selection with peripheral copies: looking at an object makes a small copy of it appear in the periphery, and a quick glance at the copy confirms the selection, avoiding the Midas touch without dwell.
howItWorks: When gaze rests on a selectable element, a context-specific virtual copy is shown at a peripheral position away from the target; a saccade to the copy confirms. Leader lines link copies to their targets when several are nearby, and the copies can also act as handles for sliders and other analogue controls. In a VR study with 17 participants, EyeShadows was significantly faster than dwell and also beat head-crossing and Duo-Reticles in some respects, with higher error in some conditions; MR versions were demonstrated on HoloLens 2 and Varjo XR-3.
advantages: Copies show what will be selected, so poor eye-tracking accuracy matters less.
limitations: Error rate was higher than the baselines in some conditions.
Peripheral copies need free space in the view.
